comparisons.peer_topic: IP Protection Strategy and Portfolio Strength
comparisons.peer_summary: Broadcom relies on patents, copyrights, trademarks, trade secrets, and contractual protections to safeguard its IP, leveraging a strong portfolio of 20,870 U.S. and other patents and 2,650 pending applications as of November 3, 2024, to develop application-specific products.
comparisons.comparison: Both AMD and Broadcom rely on intellectual property rights, including patents, copyrights, trademarks, and trade secrets, to protect their products and technologies. A key similarity is the explicit statement that neither company is substantially dependent on any single patent or group of related patents. However, they differ in the specific metrics disclosed: AMD reported approximately 18,800 patent matters worldwide (13,200 issued and 5,600 pending) as of December 2024, whereas Broadcom reported 20,870 U.S. and other patents and 2,650 U.S. and other pending patent applications as of November 2024.

sentences.text: Including United States and foreign matters, we have approximately 18,800 patent matters worldwide consisting of approximately 13,200 issued patents and 5,600 patent applications pending.
Intellectual property rights include copyrights, patents, patent applications, trademarks, trade secrets and mask work rights.
As of November 3, 2024, we had 20,870 U.S. and other patents and 2,650 U.S. and other pending patent applications.
We are not substantially dependent on any single patent or group of related patents.

comparisons.peer_summary: Intel owns and develops significant IP rights globally, including patents, copyrights, trade secrets, trademarks, and mask works, to support its products, services, R&D, and assets.
comparisons.comparison: Both AMD and Intel disclose their reliance on a significant global portfolio of intellectual property rights, including patents, copyrights, and trademarks, to support their products, services, and R&D activities. The specific composition differs: AMD explicitly lists 'mask work rights' in its IP definition, while Intel also includes 'mask works' but emphasizes 'trade secrets' alongside patents and trademarks in its general portfolio statement. Both companies view this IP portfolio as fundamental to their business operations.

sentences.text: Intellectual property rights include copyrights, patents, patent applications, trademarks, trade secrets and mask work rights.
We rely on contracts and intellectual property rights to protect our products and technologies from unauthorized third-party copying and use.
Our IP portfolio includes patents, copyrights, trade secrets, trademarks, mask works, and other rights.
We own and develop significant IP and related IP rights around the world that support our products, services, R&D, and other activities and assets.

comparisons.peer_summary: As of August 29, 2024, the company owned approximately 14,500 active U.S. patents and 7,000 active foreign patents, with terms expiring through 2043, alongside thousands of pending applications.
comparisons.comparison: Both AMD and Micron disclose specific quantitative metrics regarding their patent portfolios, including the number of issued patents and pending applications. Both companies hold thousands of patents. A key difference is the breakdown of geographic scope: Micron explicitly distinguishes between active U.S. patents (14,500) and active foreign patents (7,000), while AMD reports a consolidated global total of 18,800 patent matters (13,200 issued and 5,600 pending) without breaking out the U.S. versus foreign issued counts in the same sentence.

sentences.text: Including United States and foreign matters, we have approximately 18,800 patent matters worldwide consisting of approximately 13,200 issued patents and 5,600 patent applications pending.
As of August 29, 2024, we owned approximately 14,500 active U.S. patents and 7,000 active foreign patents.
In addition, we have thousands of U.S. and foreign patent applications pending.

comparisons.peer_summary: NVIDIA relies on patents, trademarks, trade secrets, nondisclosure agreements, and licensing arrangements to protect its IP, with issued patents expiring between February 2024 and August 2043 and numerous other patents issued, allowed, or pending globally for products and related technology.
comparisons.comparison: Both AMD and NVIDIA rely on a combination of patents, trademarks, trade secrets, and licensing arrangements to protect their intellectual property in the United States and internationally. Both companies also hold numerous patents that are issued, allowed, or pending. A difference is found in the specific details provided: NVIDIA explicitly discloses the expiration date range of its currently issued patents (February 2024 to August 2043) and mentions reliance on international treaties, whereas AMD focuses on the total count of patent matters (18,800) and expectations to file future applications.

We rely on contracts and intellectual property rights to protect our products and technologies from unauthorized third-party copying and use.

We rely primarily on a combination of patents, trademarks, trade secrets, employee and third-party nondisclosure agreements, and licensing arrangements to protect our IP in the United States and internationally.

comparisons.peer_topic: Intellectual property portfolio and technology scope
comparisons.peer_summary: The company owns significant IP in CDMA/OFDMA technologies and develops other key technologies including video/audio codecs, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, AI, machine learning, and RF/RFFE designs, some of which become industry standards.
comparisons.comparison: Both AMD and Qualcomm disclose ownership of significant intellectual property, including patents and trade secrets, to support their products. A major difference is the strategic focus: Qualcomm's IP portfolio is heavily centered on standard-essential technologies like CDMA/OFDMA, Wi-Fi, and Bluetooth, which are often contributed to industry standards. In contrast, AMD's disclosure focuses on a broader count of general patent matters (18,800 worldwide) to protect its specific product technologies from unauthorized copying, without emphasizing standard-essential patent contributions in this specific disclosure segment.

sentences.text: Including United States and foreign matters, we have approximately 18,800 patent matters worldwide consisting of approximately 13,200 issued patents and 5,600 patent applications pending.
We rely on contracts and intellectual property rights to protect our products and technologies from unauthorized third-party copying and use.
We own significant intellectual property, including patents, patent applications and trade secrets, applicable to products that implement any version of CDMA and/or OFDMA technologies.

Some of these inventions are contributed to and commercialized as industry standards, such as for certain video and audio codecs, Wi-Fi, position location, UWB (ultra-wideband), Bluetooth®, memory and component interconnect.
